claim: Normal bladder capacity is 400-600 mL (the bladder fills to roughly half a liter before fullness); chronic retention is flagged at volumes over 300 mL
Long-term urinary retention carries risk of urinary tract infection (urine stasis lets bacteria multiply in retained urine)
Untreated chronic retention/obstruction can cause bladder damage and chronic kidney failure
source URL: and back-pressure on the kidneys (hydronephrosis); acute retention is a medical emergency

claim: Bladder wall stretch receptors send the urge signal to the brain (micturition reflex); holding occasionally is tolerated - the body waits

Bladder rupture is rare and overwhelmingly follows blunt trauma or instrumentation on a full bladder; voluntary holding by a healthy person is not a documented cause ("bursting from holding" is a myth)
